svg.title: Where leakage enters a model-building pipeline
svg.desc: Six pipeline stages in two rows, connected by arrows showing the order of work. Row one: 1 collect and label, 2 split, 3 fit preprocessing. A connector leads down to row two: 4 train, 5 tune on validation, 6 test once. Amber notes mark where leakage enters: L1 a field set after the outcome, at collection; L2 one customer in two splits and L3 later months in training, at the split; L4 statistics fit on all rows, at preprocessing; training inherits whatever leaked earlier; L5 tuning against the test set, at tuning; L6 test cases reused in prompts or examples, at testing. A footer lists four checks: feature timestamp not after prediction time, no customer in two splits, preprocessing fit on training rows only, and the test set opened once.

g.text: Leakage: the score sees information the live system will not
L1 field set after the outcome
L2 one customer in two splits
L4 statistics fit on all rows
L5 tuning against the test set
Checks you can automate: feature timestamp ≤ prediction time · no customer ID in two splits ·
preprocessing fit on training rows only · test set opened once, after choices are frozen.
Arrows show the order of work. Amber notes mark leaks; each one makes the score describe the evaluation, not live traffic.
